content: Waisak (Vesak) is the Buddhist commemoration of the Buddha's birth, enlightenment, and death — celebrated on the full moon of the lunar month of Vesakha (usually May). In Indonesia the largest observance is at Borobudur: thousands of monks and pilgrims gather, meditate, and release lanterns into the night sky. The lantern release is ticketed; access to the temple upper terraces is highly restricted that day. Book lantern tickets months ahead. Public holiday nationally.

Cap Go Meh marks the 15th day (final day) of Chinese New Year celebrations, most vividly in Indonesia's Chinese-Indonesian communities — Singkawang (West Kalimantan) hosts arguably the largest, with tatung (spirit-medium) processions that draw international visitors. Also strong in Jakarta's Glodok, Semarang, Surabaya, Bogor, and Pontianak. Not a national public holiday but the underlying Imlek (Chinese New Year) is.

Erau is the annual cultural festival of the Kutai Kartanegara sultanate in Tenggarong, East Kalimantan — traditionally centred on the enthronement anniversary. Modern Erau (revived in the 1970s) runs about a week and includes Dayak dance, boat races on the Mahakam river, tepong tawar (blessing rituals), and the belimbur (mutual water-throwing) finale. Typically held in September or October.

Bau Nyale is an annual Sasak festival on Lombok's south coast (around Kuta Lombok) — thousands gather at night to catch nyale, a sea worm that surfaces once a year in February or March according to the traditional calendar. The worms are considered incarnations of the legendary Princess Mandalika. The event is preceded by a night of song, poetry (bepantun), and cultural performance. A significant recent-revival tradition tied to Sasak identity.
